memory_candidates.content: Test-fixture pitfall: `grep -c PATTERN file || echo 0` double-counts on a no-match file -- `grep -c` already prints "0" to stdout on zero matches AND exits nonzero, so a trailing `|| echo 0` fallback fires too, producing "0\n0" instead of "0". Capture grep's stdout into a variable first (`n=$(grep -c ... 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$n" ] && n=0`), independent of its exit status, rather than chaining a fallback onto the same command substitution.

To simulate "binary X is absent from PATH" in a bash test fixture while every OTHER tool a script needs (bash itself, jq, python3, coreutils) must still resolve normally: build ONE scratch directory of symlinks to everything currently reachable on PATH except files literally named X, and use that single directory as the fixture's PATH. Narrowing PATH to a minimal literal list like "/usr/bin:/bin" is NOT portable (NixOS has no /bin/bash) and silently breaks the test. Additionally, if the SAME test needs a before/after comparison (tool present vs. absent) and the script under test re-resolves some OTHER dependency fresh on every invocation (e.g. `command -v python3`), use the SAME scratch directory for both runs and only add/remove the target file between them -- using two separately-built scratch directories makes that other dependency resolve to a different absolute path each time, which can make the script under test spuriously detect "drift" that was never really there.

When coupling a per-project writer action's idempotence check to an external config map that is ALSO read elsewhere by a different (longest-prefix) matching rule, the write-side idempotence decision must use the WRITER's own key predicate, not the reader's. Concrete instance: setup-sapience-mcp.sh's --capture-set reads the EXACT-PATH capture.projects[] entry (realpath'd) to decide whether to call the vendor CLI, because set_project() itself matches/creates by exact realpath'd path_prefix -- while verify-sapience-mcp.sh's check (i) mirrors the READER's longest-prefix-wins rule for reporting. Using the reader's rule for the writer's idempotence decision would make a child repo under an enabled parent prefix never acquire its own entry.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience-mcp-register-project.sh worktree behavior
sapience_notes.value: Confirmed live (not just inferred): inside a linked git worktree that carries its own tracked .claude-extensions.json, the hook's `[ -f ".claude-extensions.json" ]` branch sets PROJECT_PATH to the WORKTREE path, not the parent checkout -- resolve_checkout_toplevel()'s GIT_ROOT correctly resolves to the checkout instead. Any future per-project write keyed on activation status must use GIT_ROOT, never PROJECT_PATH, when invoked from inside a worktree.

sapience_notes.subject: setup-sapience-mcp.sh resolve_interpreter()
sapience_notes.value: resolve_interpreter() only ever inherits a previously-written interpreter path from the TOP-LEVEL global .mcpServers.sapience.command key -- never from a project-scoped .projects[path].mcpServers.sapience.command entry, which this writer actually writes by default (--scope project). So for an ordinary project-scoped registration, every single invocation re-resolves python3 fresh via `command -v python3`, regardless of what was written on a prior run. A test or diagnostic that runs this writer twice under two DIFFERENT PATH environments (even both containing a valid python3) will see the interpreter command field change between runs.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience config.json folders list and capture.projects[]
sapience_notes.value: ~/.sapience/config.json's legacy top-level folders list is evaluated BEFORE capture.projects[] in the vendor's extraction pipeline (_session_candidates()'s folder-name filter, and sync()'s bail when folders == []). The `sapience projects on|off` CLI never touches folders. There is no safe, non-interactive, single-writer path to grow it: the vendor's own onboarding chooser refuses without a TTY, and SAPIENCE_ALLOW_ONBOARD=1 overwrites the entire saved selection rather than appending. An enabled:true capture.projects[] entry is therefore not, by itself, evidence that a repository's transcripts are actually being read.

sapience_notes.subject: SAPIENCE_NO_CAPTURE_SYNC guard
sapience_notes.value: Re-confirmed live on this machine: the SAPIENCE_NO_CAPTURE_SYNC=1 guard is present at ~/.sapience/upload.py:1023 and causes projects_cli's trailing capture_sync() call to return before any HTTP request, making `sapience projects on|off <path>` network-free when that variable is set.

sapience_notes.subject: agent-system/extensions/sapience index-entries.json drift
sapience_notes.value: A plan's own stated premise about a derived quantity (index-entries.json's line_count for per-repo-scoping.md, claimed as 410 at plan-authoring time) can itself be stale by the time implementation runs: the live value at this task's Phase 5 start was already 618, not 410 -- a premise drift from an earlier dispatch rather than a concurrent sibling edit. Always re-read a derived quantity live immediately before trusting a plan's stated baseline for it, even when the plan explicitly says the baseline 'matches the file's live length.'

sapience_notes.subject: grep -c on a no-match file
sapience_notes.value: POSIX grep -c prints "0" to stdout on a file with zero matches AND still exits with status 1 (no match found). A bash idiom of `n=$(grep -c PATTERN file || echo 0)` therefore prints "0\n0" on a no-match file, not "0", because the || fallback fires on top of grep's own already-correct zero output.
